## Where GoAI sits among prior work

The authors make three positioning claims.

- **Educational knowledge graphs** (e.g., EDUKG for K–12, MOOC concept-recommendation work) mostly integrate *static* knowledge. They pay little attention to synthesizing research literature or supporting student innovation.
- **AI idea-generation systems** typically use research *trend chains* or academic graphs. GoAI instead keeps a graph and adds citation semantics and citation importance.
- **Combining graphs with LLMs** can be done by feeding GNN-processed graph information into the model, or by turning triples into text prompts. GoAI takes the second route. Its reason is that papers and the relation labels are already natural language, so the graph can simply be written out as text, much like retrieval-augmented generation.

This last choice shapes the rest of the method. The LLM never sees embeddings of graph structure. It reads descriptions of papers and relations and picks among them.
